history.dynasty: Koch dynasty (rebuilt 1583 CE by Raghudeva Narayan) over 10th-11th century foundations; 19th-century restoration under Kalia Bhomora Borphukan's family
history.period: Ancient site mentioned in the 11th-century Kalika Purana; present stone structure completed 1583 CE
history.summary: The Hayagriva Madhava Temple is the famous Vaishnava shrine on Manikut hill at Hajo, dedicated to Vishnu as Hayagriva, the horse-headed avatar who restored the Vedas stolen from Brahma by the demons Madhu and Kaitabha. The site is praised in the 11th-century Kalika Purana; the present stone structure was rebuilt in 1583 CE by Koch king Raghudeva Narayan over the ruins of a 10th-11th century temple (ASI/NMA record). Travel sources report that an earlier structure was destroyed by Kalapahar (unverified). The Nagara-style temple is celebrated for its continuous frieze of elephants along the base — likened to Ellora — and outer-wall reliefs of the ten avatars of Vishnu and scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata; the nearby Madhab Pukhuri tank adds to the precinct. Sayani, first wife of Kalia Bhomora Borphukan, donated land and a family of paiks during Ahom king Kamaleswar Singha's reign; a Doul Griha in the complex is attributed to Ahom king Pramatta Singha (c.1750, per one source). The akhanda deep (eternal lamp) in the garbhagriha is said never to be extinguished. Tibetan and Mahayana Buddhists revere the hill as the Buddha's parinirvana site, making it a shared Hindu-Buddhist pilgrimage centre; it is an ASI-protected living monument. CSV CORRECTION: the town 'Nagaon' is WRONG — the temple is at Hajo, Kamrup district (about 30 km west of Guwahati); no Hayagriva Madhav Mandir was found in Nagaon district. Corrected to Hajo, Kamrup. Coordinates are a full-address geocode match for the temple.

name: Hayagriva Madhava Temple
town_description: Hajo, in Kamrup district about 30 km west of Guwahati, is an ancient pilgrimage town sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Muslims alike. Its three hillocks carry the Hayagriva Madhava temple (Manikut), the Kedareswara Shiva temple (Madanchala) and the Poa Mecca dargah (Garurachala), making it one of Assam's oldest centres of faith.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati (approx. 30-35 km).
travel.road: Well connected by road from Guwahati; the temple stands atop Manikut hill and is reached by a flight of stone steps.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Doul Utsav and Janmashtami draw large crowds and are the most vibrant times to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily as a living ASI-protected monument; exact darshan hours are not published online — verify locally before travel.
